title: A Decellularization Methodology for the Production of a Natural Acellular Intestinal Matrix
protocol: Prepare a 1 L solution of Phosphate Buffered Saline with 1% antibiotic/antimycotic.
Run 70% ethanol through the tubes of the peristaltic pump for 15 min at maximum speed.
Continue running PBS/AA through the tubes for another 15 min.
Euthanize adult Sprague-Dawley rats by CO2 inhalation and cervical dislocation.
Autoclave surgical instruments before use.
Spray and wipe the abdomen of the animal using 70% ethanol.
Perform a xifo-pubic laparotomic incision on the abdomen to ensure a clear surgical field.
Eviscerate the small intestine onto a paper towel sprayed with 70% ethanol.
Wet the intestine continuously with PBS/AA to avoid dehydration and denaturation of ECM.
Locate the superior mesenteric artery arising in a 90° angle from the aorta towards the intestine.
Use a 27 G cannula to enter the SMA from the aorta and quickly withdraw the needle.
Advance the plastic tube of the cannula into the SMA and secure using sutures.
Confirm cannulation by injecting 1 ml of PBS/AA.
Use spring scissors to incise the aorta proximal and distal to the SMA to release the cannula.
Place one silk suture knot (5/0) on the proximal end of the ileocaecal junction.
Place one silk suture knot (5/0) on the distal end of the sigmoid colon.
Cut the terminal ileum and colon between the two knots.
Remove the large intestine.
Cut the intestine at the jejuno-duodenal junction.
Free the intestine from any connective tissue connections it might have with the abdomen.
Transfer the small intestine in a Petri dish with PBS/AA.
Cannulate the proximal section of the intestine with a plastic Pasteur pipette (LSL Laboratory Consumables).
Secure the cannula in place with sutures.
Cut the pipette so it will fit the Luer-Lok of a 60 ml syringe (BD Plastipak).
Flush the intestinal lumen twice with 60 ml of PBS/AA to remove feces and debris.
Connect the vascular cannula to a three-way stopcock.
Start running deionized water through the Masterflex L/S variable speed roller pump at 0.6 ml/hr.
Ensure no bubbles are present within the tubing prior to connecting with the intestinal lumen stopcock.
Handle the tissue carefully with forceps to ensure bubbles exit from the distal end.
Transfer apparatus to the cold room for decellularization, which is performed at 4 °C.
Place the Petri dish in a container that will collect the overflowing solution.
Perfuse both the intestinal lumen and the vascular tree with deionized water (resistivity 18.2 MΩ/cm) for 24 hr at 0.6 ml/hr.
Check the apparatus regularly during the first hour to ensure all connections are secure, leakage is minimal, and no bubbles are present within the intestine.
Move decellularization apparatus outside the cold room after 24 hr of treatment with deionized water.
Weigh sodium deoxycholate under a suction hood.
Mix sodium deoxycholate with deionized water to prepare a 4% solution.
Vortex the solution until clear.
Maintain the solution at 4°C for up to 1 month.
Perfuse scaffold with sodium deoxycholate solution at 0.6 ml/hr for 4 hr.
Wash scaffold with PBS/AA for 30 min.
Weigh out DNase-I and prepare a 2,000 kU solution in 1 M sodium chloride, pH 7.4.
Mix DNase-I solution until clear.
Perfuse scaffold with DNase-I solution at RT at 0.6 ml/hr for 3 hr.
Transfer scaffold to tissue culture hood after DNase-I perfusion.
Wash scaffold with PBS/AA for 30 min.
Place scaffold in a new Petri dish and transfer to a UV Crosslinker.
Run two sterilization cycles on the scaffold.
Store scaffold in 5% PBS/AA.
Change storage solution every 3 days.
